impl.summary: World mode on your GPU. Cinema gets a World take: you write the opening (the world in words, who the camera follows, the camera and the look), then add turns. Each turn has what changes, what the subject does, a camera move from the fly-path library (or Still) and 3-12 s. The panel has Run turn, Redo from here (the turns before it stay), a top-down view of the camera path, Export (the turns joined into one film on the open engine's packet join) and links to Sound for video and Music, because Hy-Nomas makes no sound. It runs on Hy-Nomas (Tencent, Apache-2.0) through Nynxz's ComfyUI-HyNomas port, which is pinned with its converted weights. The new pure converter src/lib/world-path.ts turns Fuobe camera paths into Tencent's trajectory (OpenCV c2ws plus normalised intrinsics at 24 fps, gains 1.0 / 2.5) and into the key script the port reads. Assist gets world_film ('a 60 s walk-through' = the opening plus four 12 s turns). There is a GPU pre-flight row 'World mode' and licence rows. Open engine only: the cloud says it runs on your GPU, and 'Paid APIs only' hides the World chip. fal's worlds models are recorded in research as different models. Nothing from the plan existed before; the camera-path library (src/lib/camera-path.ts framePoses / presets, N7-5) was reused.
built: Port and weights: packs.json pins ComfyUI-HyNomas at a89e0515 (Apache-2.0, no Python deps, not in the Comfy Registry) and install-comfyui.sh installs it. model-pins.json pins nynxz/Hy-Nomas at e8ddc4bf with sha256: int8 ConvRot DiT 8.97 GB, PixelUMM VAE 15.78 GB, and the bf16 DiT 17.11 GB as optional. The text encoder qwen_2.5_vl_7b was already pinned (Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image) and is shared, so the new files come to about 24.8 GB. library.spec.mjs has PACK_CLASSES and KNOWN_MODELS entries. object_info.subset.json has the 6 Nomas node definitions, written by hand from nomas/nodes.py at the pin. manifest.json and requirements.json were rebuilt (validated:false, like the other packs that are not on the validation server).

History between /prompt calls: the port keeps a world in ComfyUI's memory (the NOMAS_WORLD output plus an int8 KV cache in temp/nomas_history). Separate prompts share it only through ComfyUI's output cache, or through the Nomas Explore node's in-process sessions, which only accept keyboard input. So the graph world-hy-nomas-turn (scripts/comfy/hand-built, based on the port's nomas_world example) is rebuilt per run by src/lib/world.ts expandWorldWorkflow (expand:'world'). It holds the opening plus one NomasWorldContinue per turn up to k, with stable node ids and inputs, then TrimVideoLatent cuts off the earlier turns' latents, then VAEDecode, CreateVideo 24 fps and SaveVideo. So turn k decodes only its own frames, and ComfyUI reuses turns 0..k-1 while it still holds them. If it doesn't (another job ran, or a restart), it makes them again from the script's fixed seed and gets the same world. This is the 'whole film as N turns' fallback, made incremental.

src/lib/world-path.ts: worldTrajectory (the turns chained, each starting where the last stopped), worldIntrinsic (fx=f/W, fy=f/H, cx=cy=0.5 as generate_npz_trajectories.py writes them), WORLD_SCALES {translation 1.0, rotation 2.5}, turnPoses. steerTicks/worldScripts fly a simulation of the port's Pose (W/S along the view, A/D strafe, arrows at 20°/s, mouse at 0.0024 rad/px) along the path in closed loop. Mouse-drag ticks catch up turns faster than the arrows can, and the heading carries from turn to turn. ticksScript/parseScript write and read the port's script; pathSketch gives the preview.

src/lib/world.ts: the script model (opening plus turns, seed), limits (3-12 s in 0.5 s steps, 10 turns, 120 s), the port's latent arithmetic (turnLatents/latentsBefore/clipSeconds), subject → <|Subject1|>, turn state (scriptKey, clipsFromTakes with Redo-from-here cut-offs, nextTurn, canRun, redoFrom, exportClips) and the graph expansion.

Catalog: new op 'world-turn' (types, labels, output video, PROMPTLESS, script check in planGeneration). New model oss-hy-nomas-world (open, hidden from the studio menus, comfy route world-hy-nomas-turn). The comfyui provider reads params.extra.world/turn, always uses the script's seed, and expands the graph.

Cinema: CinemaAction 'world' with planWorld (open only: the cloud gets WORLD_OPEN_ONLY and no stand-in; notes; free) and Export through oss-join-encoded. The take remembers {turn, script, made, joined}. cinema-schemas has WorldSchema. Redo from here with unchanged words gives the same turn, because the port's noise is a seeded bank. A different take needs changed words or a changed move; the button's tooltip says so. A per-turn re-roll would need a port change.

The port only reads camera poses, not intrinsics: worldIntrinsic exists for Tencent's .npz form, and Fuobe doesn't run Tencent's runtime. Keys can't rise straight up, so height changes are flown along the tilted view.
The 24 GB VRAM figure is a guess. Tencent's 4090 configuration uses an FP8 decoder, which the port doesn't ship (it refuses Tencent's int8 file).

docsNotes: The brief named the text encoder as 'Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI'. The pinned qwen_2.5_vl_7b.safetensors actually comes from Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image @1f12b17b, which was already in KNOWN_MODELS. The fp8_scaled variant lives in Qwen-Image_ComfyUI.
Brief out of date or unclear: the 'trajectory file' is what Tencent's runtime reads; the ComfyUI port reads WASD/mouse scripts (NomasCameraPath) instead, so the converter produces both.

Licence correction: Hy-Nomas itself is Apache-2.0, but the PixelUMM decoder weights (which both the converted and Tencent's files are) are under the NVIDIA One-Way Noncommercial License per nynxz's card. The PE is in Tencent's Apache-2.0 repo (~55 GB, 18 shards) and is not used.

findings.summary: The browser matches a turn's clip against the raw script it is editing, but the server stamps the take with the key of the cleaned-up script. When the two differ, a turn that finished correctly shows as 'Changed: run it again'. The next turn and Export then stay blocked until the page is reloaded.
findings.failure_scenario: Write the opening as 'A forest at dusk. ' (a trailing space, or a newline at the end of the textarea) and press Run the opening. worldTake (src/lib/catalog/cinema.ts:2572) builds `made` with scriptKey(normalizeWorld(script)), and normalizeWorld trims the words. The panel calls clipsFromTakes(w, …) with the untrimmed state `w`, so scriptKey(w,0) !== take.made. The result is clips=[undefined] and states=['stale']. Checked two ways. A scratch vitest probe returned made===key false and states ['stale']. A demo-mode browser probe on :3417 showed 'Changed: run it again' and no 'Ready' after the opening's take succeeded. The same mismatch happens for leading or trailing spaces in the subject, details, action or turn words, and for a typed length that isn't a half-second step (4.3 s is rounded to 4.5 on the server). A reload hides the problem only because restore() normalises the stored script. Fix: key and send the normalised script on the client (normalizeWorld(w) for clipsFromTakes, input() and plan), or compare keys after normalising both sides. Add a test with untrimmed words.

findings.summary: Each turn's latents are trimmed and decoded alone. The PixelUMM decoder then starts every turn with no earlier latents as context, and its window noise is seeded from absolute frame 0 instead of the turn's real offset. The exported join can therefore show a visible seam at every turn boundary.
findings.failure_scenario: Read in the port at a89e0515. integration.PixelUMMVAE.decode calls pixelumm.decode_clip(latent), which runs decode_windows with offset=0. The port's own continuation path, decode_tail, re-decodes STRIDE=5 latents before the new frames, passes offset=start and cross-fades the overlap 'for continuity'. TrimVideoLatent → VAEDecode skips both, so frame 0 of turn k is decoded cold. oss-join-encoded joins packets without re-encoding, so nothing smooths the cut. This can't be checked without a GPU. The 'left' list mentions the 5D decode as unverified, but not the seam. Possible fix: trim to latentsBefore−5, then cut the first 20 pixel frames after decode, so the decoder gets the port's context.

findings.summary: Redo-from-here cut-offs (redoAt) live only in component state. After the panel is closed or the page reloaded, the takes made before the redo count as current clips for the later turns again.
findings.failure_scenario: Turns 0–2 are done. Press Redo from here on turn 1 and close or reload before turn 2 is re-run. clipsFromTakes loses redoAt, and the old turn-2 take still matches scriptKey (the script is unchanged), so it shows as Ready and goes into Export. The harm is small today, because the port's noise is seeded and an unchanged redo gives identical frames. It still contradicts the button's promise. Each turn's 'films this turn again and the ones after it' should survive a reload, for example stored with the script in localStorage or as a take field.

review.verdict: changes-requested: the build is sound against the port and pins, tsc is clean and the targeted tests and the browser check pass. One confirmed medium bug needs fixing first: the World panel compares its raw script with the server's normalised script key, so ordinary input such as trailing spaces leaves a finished turn showing 'Changed: run it again' and blocks the next turn and Export until a reload. applied: Finding 1 (medium, confirmed): the World panel's turn state no longer goes stale when the fields have stray spaces or a length off the half second. scriptKey in src/lib/world.ts now keys normalizeWorld(script), so the browser's key and the server's take key (worldTake) agree. The panel (src/components/cinema/world-panel.tsx) also works from the tidied script for everything it sends, keys and checks: clipsFromTakes, nextTurn, canRun, exportClips, worldProblem, the plan, the request body, the totals, the timeline and the path sketch. Finding 3 (low, confirmed): Redo from here now survives closing the panel or reloading. clipsFromTakes only counts a turn's take if it was made after the current clips of the turns before it, because the world continues from those clips. So once a redone turn has a newer take, the later turns' older takes stop counting, and this is worked out from the takes themselves with nothing stored. If a redo fails, the earlier film stands. The in-memory redoAt still covers the moment before the new take shows up. New unit test covers a reload after a redo, a running redo and a failed redo.
rejected: Finding 2 (low, plausible: possible decode seams at turn boundaries, because each turn's latents are trimmed and decoded with no context and the decoder's window noise starts at offset 0). Not changed. It can't be checked without a GPU. The suggested fix would change the trim arithmetic, which is currently checked against the port, and would add a pixel-frame cut whose size depends on PixelUMM's undocumented causal frame layout for a decode that starts partway through. The noise offset can't be set through stock nodes at all. Recorded in 'left' to settle on the first live GPU run.
